evidence.quote: What happened was we had a cascading failure that started around 11 PM on the 10th and by about 5 AM on the 11th we had essentially zero threat monitoring visibility for customers on the Detect module.
The last event we see in the dashboard is timestamped at 7:14 AM this morning and it is now almost 10:30 and I have a team of analysts sitting here staring at a dead screen.
We're implementing redundant processing nodes and we're adding a circuit breaker pattern so that if one node degrades, traffic gets redistributed rather than causing a full outage.
The part I'm less sure about is how the redundant node setup interacts with our current Kafka config. We haven't fully mapped that out yet.
I think we need to add redundant processing nodes and probably implement a circuit breaker pattern to prevent cascading failures.
Okay, so on my end this week — I finished deploying the second set of redundant processing nodes for Detect.

evidence.quote: So with Comply v2 — and this just went GA two days ago, April 7th — we've built out on-demand reporting that's fully mapped to PCI DSS controls.

And we just — we really want to know if there's any way to get early access before the general release because our SOC 2 audit window is coming up and the timing would be really helpful.

Great — so, big news, and I mean this is actually really good timing for you guys, Comply v2 went GA literally today, April 7th, so you are among the very first customers to be onboarding onto the new version.

evidence.quote: If your certificate was issued by an internal certificate authority, our connector doesn't inherently trust that CA. You need to upload your internal CA's root certificate into Aegis Identity so that we can validate the chain.

We rotated our SAML signing certificate yesterday, standard procedure, we do this every six months, and after the rotation a significant portion of our users are getting authentication failures when they try to SSO into our internal tools.
So basically, we push policy updates through Identity — role assignments, access group changes — and they're just... not propagating.

So it started, um, I'd say around 7 AM this morning, and it's not all users — it seems to be specifically the users who are enrolled in TOTP-based MFA through Aegis Identity, they're getting token validation failures even though the tokens are generating correctly on their authenticator apps.
About 38 to 42 percent of our user base is hitting the failure.
So the session timeout is set globally right now, and we can't scope it by device group or location.

evidence.quote: It says — let me actually pull it up — it says, uh, 'connector write operation terminated, upstream response code 403.'
